caption:
If you simply pick up and go instead of shifting your center of mass backward during your leg lift, it creates several issues that can hurt velo and add stress to your arm:

1) You limit momentum and get pushy off the back leg.

2) You don’t create rhythm with your glove and front leg.

3) Your arm is playing “catch up” because of the quick body move.
alt: Video by Denny Brady | CPT, CNC, CFSC on August 25, 2026.
transcript: So you set up in an athletic position and then the first move has to be to get your weight to shift backwards. Instead you just pick up and get moving right away. One, you don't have that shift of your center of mass so you're gonna have less momentum and less power going down the mound. And two, your arm is going to be playing catch up because your body's moving so quickly. So this initial move one is to shift the momentum, but two it's to get rhythm with the front leg and glove moving together. If you just pick up and go, you have no rhythm, you're losing momentum, your arms playing catch up. Plus you're gonna have much less power to work with out of the back leg, so guess what's gonna have to work harder?
